context_documents.title: 2023-1325 · Remote wrist actuation and practiced direct pickup avoid a second collector
context_documents.body:
# 2023-1325: Remote wrist actuation and practiced direct pickup avoid a second collector

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A small square chassis carries a shoulder/elbow/wrist arm with low-mounted transmissions and a remote aircraft-cable wrist drive. Fixed gripper spacing handles both pieces. A separate Rapid React-style collector was prototyped but not adopted; arm motion uses waypoint/path-following ideas related to the drivetrain tools.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team connects chassis size to maneuverability and says the added collector was unnecessary after substantial practice with the existing gripper, with integration and retraining costs outweighing expected benefit.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A theoretical faster acquisition mechanism can be a worse late-season choice if it consumes development and driver time without improving full-cycle reliability. Remote cable drive reduces distal motor mass but makes tension, stretch and backlash important. Safe endpoint waypoints also do not certify the swept volume between them.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure wrist hysteresis, arm clearance throughout each path, and direct-pickup performance under realistic misalignment before reviving the rejected collector.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/MfCjXe5dfOk](https://youtu.be/MfCjXe5dfOk)

source_reviews.title: 1325 Inverse Paradox | Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.facts: Identifies wrist iterations, custom VP gearbox additions, multiple Limelights, custom pathing UI, and first use of swerve.
source_reviews.limitations: Publisher summary only. No team explanation transcribed in the post.

source_reviews.title: 1325 Inverse Paradox pit interview
source_reviews.locator: Base dossier and focused technical supplement
source_reviews.review_basis: Inherited interview synopsis. Captions were not recovered in this review.
source_reviews.facts: Reports a compact square chassis, two-joint arm, aircraft-cable wrist transmission and a final fixed-spacing roller gripper.
source_reviews.limitations: Specific geometry, transmission and chronology remain inherited claims.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: The 1325 dossier describes a small swerve robot that uses the same tool to acquire and score. The arm moves through shoulder and elbow joints, with a separate wrist for orienting the piece. The noteworthy iteration is at the contact interface. The retained account says the team removed a gripping degree of freedom after learning that fixed spacing could accommodate both 2023 pieces. The interview announcement independently confirms wrist iterations and custom gearbox work at a broad level.
piece_flow: Present the tool at the supply pose and draw the piece into the roller gap. In the final configuration described by the dossier the gap is fixed.
Hold the piece in the same tool while shoulder, elbow and wrist move the piece toward the grid. The earlier collector concept is a prototype lineage.
Orient and release at the node, then retract while keeping the tool and retained piece clear of field and robot structure.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The older description puts the gearboxes low and drives the wrist remotely with aircraft cable. This can keep mass out of the distal assembly and reduce shoulder inertia. It introduces a cable route whose effective length and tension must remain stable as other joints move. On the reported 26-inch square base, extension moves the loaded center of mass toward the edge quickly, especially under braking.

subsystems.name: Fixed-spacing roller tool
subsystems.construction: Older dossier describes a static final gap and powered rollers.
subsystems.operation: Capture either piece with contact geometry and roller compliance, then carry it directly.
subsystems.team_rationale: The retained account says testing showed fixed spacing worked after opening and closing versions were tried.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A fixed gap removes a clamp action and its controls. That benefit depends on the two pieces sharing a usable compression range at their actual orientations.
subsystems.interfaces: Wrist angle controls approach and release. Contact geometry determines where the piece sits relative to wrist presets.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check whether wear and deformation cause loss of retention at one end of the size range. Test recovery from a half-seated cone.
subsystems.unknowns: Roller profile, compression, sensor and release logic.

subsystems.name: Shoulder, elbow and remote wrist
subsystems.construction: Low gearbox packaging and cable drive are inherited. The publisher explicitly mentions gearbox additions.
subsystems.operation: Move the elbow and shoulder to position the wrist while the wrist adjusts the tool angle.
subsystems.team_rationale: Specific rationale for the transmission layout needs the team interview or drawings.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A distal mass reduction trades against cable stretch, friction and pretension. Measure tool angle at the same command after reversing direction under load.
subsystems.interfaces: Shoulder and elbow motion can change cable routing clearance and loads on the distal joint.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check cable anchoring and tension before retuning a controller that appears to have pose-dependent error.
subsystems.unknowns: Cable routing, reductions, joint stops and counterbalance mounting.

subsystems.name: Approach and path controls
subsystems.construction: The publisher identifies first-season swerve, multiple Limelights and a custom pathing UI.
subsystems.operation: Older synopsis assigns vision to AprilTag and cone-node alignment.
subsystems.team_rationale: Exact camera placement rationale remains inherited and incompletely documented.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Different camera viewpoints can address different occlusion cases. Measure target visibility with the arm up and the piece seated.
subsystems.interfaces: Tool reach and yaw tolerance determine how much chassis alignment error the arm can absorb.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Verify camera alignment after remount and compare against repeatable manual fallback approaches.
subsystems.unknowns: Camera layout, steering logic and station engagement.

revisions: The inherited account places slider and pivot prototypes before a spring-closing competition design, then fixed spacing after the second event and a later gas-spring counterbalance. Exact installation dates remain open.
transferable_principles: Compare cycle time and release scatter on a fixed tool before allocating a clamp actuator. Test remote wrist accuracy at several arm angles with the piece installed.
disconfirming_conditions: Fixed spacing loses its advantage if worn contacts cannot retain the smallest piece while still admitting the largest. Remote drive loses value if loaded hysteresis consumes the placement tolerance.
remaining_gaps: Team-authored mechanism text, full captions, installed version dates and station behavior.
recommended_images: Seek a side view of the complete cable route and side-by-side images of opening and fixed grippers.
